_readme: Evidence for Seedance 2.5.
C2b UPDATE. C2a recorded Runware as the only surface serving this model. That is no
longer true: fal serves it on three routes, and fal is the surface CineBraid already
dispatches to. The fal schema is recorded below as a SURFACE fact and changes nothing
about the model - the ceilings, the reference counts and the seed all still come from
provider pages rather than from ByteDance.
It also does NOT make Seedance dispatchable, and the reason is the gap already named
at the bottom of this file. fal states that a reference-to-video prompt cites its
inputs as [Image1], [Video1], [Audio1]. That is one provider sentence about how to
WRITE for a model, which is the one kind of claim this catalogue refuses to promote:
a prompting playbook is CineBraid's own editorial policy built on vendor guidance, and
building one on a single line of a provider page would be a guess with a version
number on it. So the fal offering stays `catalogued`, no model pack was written, and
the capability-aware picker says exactly that.
A split record, and worth reading as the example of what vendor-partial means.
ByteDance Seed's own product page establishes what the model IS - thirty seconds in
one pass, reference video understood as framing and cinematic intent, timestamp-level
editing. It publishes no parameter schema. BytePlus ModelArk, which does, serves its
documentation through client-side rendering and returned only navigation.
So the numbers - reference counts, the duration range, seed, audio - come from
Runware's model page and are recorded as what a PROVIDER accepts. Resolution is left
null on the model because the two sources disagree and neither is a model-level
statement CineBraid has read.

sources.note: A PROVIDER source. Admissible for surface facts and, where flagged, for capability figures no vendor source publishes.

surfaceFacts.claim: fal serves Seedance 2.5 on text-to-video, image-to-video and reference-to-video.
First/last-frame is an optional end_image_url on the image-to-video route, not a separate endpoint - structurally identical to MiniMax H3 on the same provider.
Duration is a string, 'auto' or whole seconds from 4 to 30.

Aspect ratio is available on every route including image-to-video, with an 'auto' member - which is a real divergence from MiniMax H3 on the same provider, where the image route has no ratio field at all.
References are capped at 50 in total across images, videos and audio.
Audio generation is a boolean, default true.
A seed is accepted and returned with the result.

identity.note: ByteDance states 2.5 extends single-pass generation from 15 to 30 seconds, which is what establishes 2.0 as superseded.

capabilities.claim: Single-pass generation up to 30 seconds, extendable twice.
Multiple logically connected shots can be organised inside one generation.
Reference video is understood as intention, framing and cinematic language rather than motion to copy.
Timestamp-level control for targeted audio and video editing.
Frame images for first and last position.

capabilities.note: PROVIDER FIGURE; the 30 agrees with the vendor page.

capabilities.claim: Audio generation is supported and enabled by default.

capabilities.note: PROVIDER FIGURE. No ByteDance source read confirms it.

notEstablished.status: Runware serves 480p and 720p; ByteDance describes higher output. No vendor parameter list was read.
notEstablished.cineBraidBehaviour: constraints.resolutions is null on the model and the 480p/720p ceiling is recorded against the Runware offering only.

notEstablished.status: Runware states frames are duration multiplied by the model's fps and does not disclose the fps
notEstablished.cineBraidBehaviour: constraints.fps is null and no quantiser is asserted.

notEstablished.claim: The reference-citation syntax used in prompts.
notEstablished.status: ByteDance publishes a Seedance 2.5 prompt guide. It could not be retrieved. C2b found one provider sentence - fal's reference-to-video page describes citing inputs as [Image1], [Video1], [Audio1] - which is a provider's account of how to write for someone else's model.
notEstablished.cineBraidBehaviour: promptPolicy.state is still not-established, and no model pack was written in C2b. This remains the single most consequential gap for this model: a reference-heavy model whose citation syntax rests on one provider line cannot be compiled to, and no syntax has been guessed. Closing it means reading ByteDance's own prompt guide.

notEstablished.claim: How fal splits its 50-reference total between images, video and audio.
notEstablished.status: fal documents the combined ceiling and no per-modality split. Runware's separate offering documents 30/10/10, which is Runware's figure and not fal's.
notEstablished.cineBraidBehaviour: The fal offering records maxTotal only. Copying Runware's split onto fal would be one provider's number wearing another provider's name.

notEstablished.claim: Whether audio may be the only reference input.
notEstablished.cineBraidBehaviour: No audioRequiresVisual rule is asserted for this family, unlike MiniMax H3 where the vendor states one.

conflicts.resolution: Neither written into the other. The provider's ceiling belongs to the provider; the model records nothing it cannot cite.
